title: Make release, migration, contribution, and supply-chain expectations explicit
desired_change: Add versioning and compatibility policy, ADRs, changelog, release manifest, rollback/compensation plan, migration ledger, license, contributing guide, security policy, code of conduct or explicit alternative, dependency pinning, action SHA pinning, artifact attestations, and contributor verification steps.
expected_outcome: A contributor can legally use the repository, understand change history, review migration impact, verify build inputs, and release without asking Bryan what 'done' means.

risk.rights_or_safety_impact: Ambiguous licensing, mutable dependencies, and undocumented migrations increase legal, security, and operational risk.

hidden_context_dependencies: The public repository has no license, contributing guide, security policy, changelog, release manifest, or ADR directory.
No compatibility or deprecation policy exists for protocol and schema versions.
No migration file accompanies planned database projection.
GitHub Actions use mutable major tags.
No artifact attestation or release receipt implementation exists.
No documented reviewer or branch-protection requirements exist.
acceptance_checks: A release candidate resolves version, migration, rollback, authority, eval, and receipt references.
Actions and dependencies are pinned according to documented policy.
A security reporter has a documented channel.
License and contribution terms are explicit.
Protocol and schema compatibility rules are tested.
